extracted.intended_audience: writers, editors, students, and journalism professionals (journalists, newsroom staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance from the Associated Press Stylebook (2017) for producing and editing news and journalistic content, covering grammar, usage, punctuation, capitalization, numerals, topic-specific coverage, social media, and a briefing on media law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental guidelines for spelling, language, punctuation, usage and journalistic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides fundamental guidelines for spelling, language, punctuation, usage and journalistic style. It is the definitive resource for journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: "Updated regularly since its initial publication in 1953, the AP Stylebook is a must-have reference for writers, editors, students and professionals. It provides fundamental guidelines for spelling, language, punctuation, usage and journalistic style. It is the definitive resource for journalists."

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, abbreviation, word and numeral usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed rules on grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, abbreviation, and word and numeral usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: "this 2017 edition contains more than 3,000 A to Z entries -- including more than 200 new ones -- detailing the AP's rules on grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, abbreviation, and word and numeral usage." (indicates scope and that entries explain specific rules)

rubrics_metrics.name: A-to-Z stylebook entries (entry-level guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizes style rules as A-to-Z entries covering individual words, usages, and style decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book contains more than 3,000 A to Z entries; the page lists 'Key to stylebook entries' in the table of contents, indicating guidance on how entries are presented and interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key to stylebook entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of how to read and apply the stylebook entries (the 'key' to entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the table of contents as 'Key to stylebook entries' — implies meta-guidance on interpreting entry notation, abbreviations, and conventions used throughout the AP Stylebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Style rules and conventions specific to broadcast journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the table of contents as 'Broadcast guidelines' — indicates specialized guidance for writing and editing for radio/TV broadcast formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Style and usage guidance tailored to business reporting and business journalism topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Business guidelines' in the table of contents, signaling topic-specific rules for business coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data journalism guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reporting and presenting data-driven journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Data journalism' in the table of contents; implies standards for data presentation, terminology, and reporting practices in data journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fashion guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Style guidance specific to fashion reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the table of contents as 'Fashion guidelines' — topic-specific conventions for fashion coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Style guidance for food reporting and journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Food guidelines' in the table of contents, indicating specialized usage and style rules for food coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reporting on religion, religious terminology, and related sensitivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Religion guidelines' in the table of contents; signals guidance on respectful and accurate religion reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Style and usage rules for sports reporting and related terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Sports guidelines' in the table of contents — topic-specific rules for sports coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation guide
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated guide to punctuation rules and conventions used in AP style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed separately as 'Punctuation guide' in the table of contents, distinct from general punctuation entries — likely a consolidated reference for punctuation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing on media law
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal guidance for journalists covering libel, privacy, public records, and other media law topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the table of contents as 'Briefing on media law' and in the title of the item; indicates the book contains a legal primer or reference on press law relevant to newsroom practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP statement of news values and principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The AP's articulated news values and principles that guide coverage decisions and ethical reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the table of contents as 'AP statement of news values and principles' — provides evaluative principles beyond pure style (what to cover and how to weigh newsworthiness).

rubrics_metrics.name: AP social media guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for using social media in journalistic practice, including posting, attribution, and verification on social platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'AP social media guidelines' in the table of contents — signals rules for newsroom social accounts, sourcing, and social-platform conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference of copy-editing marks and conventions for editors to mark up copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the table of contents as 'Editing marks' — provides standardized symbols and instructions for editorial workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography and index (reference/supporting material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical references and an index to support the stylebook's entries and further reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes: 'Includes bibliographical references (pages 515-517) and index' — supporting material for research and cross-referencing entries.
